content.comment_body: Hello, I'm working on a program and need help: I have 4 switches (inputs) and only one will be ON at any time. Each switch should let me select and set a different value, which I reference using counters that can be adjusted via a custom menu. How do I use the selected counter with its configured value for another part of my program, or is there a better way? I need to change the value of one counter by using the 4 switches, for example, switch 1 sets the value to 40, switch 2 to 50, etc. I've checked multiple examples but haven't found a solution. Thanks!
What do you plan to achieve with your program? I believe using an analog multiplexer could help. If you provide more details about your goal, I can offer more specific assistance.

Analog functionality in the samples appears complex, but the other features in [product_name] are straightforward and practical. The program is intended to control a motor running in one direction, using a counter to count the wheel's RPMs. I need to set 3 or 4 selectable options for how many rotations the motor should do, adjustable via the 4 switches. Only one switch will be ON at a time, and the selection is made remotely over a web interface with controllable switches. Thank you.
The approach suggested earlier is correct. You should interlock the inputs to ensure only one switch can be ON at a time.
Thank you for guiding me! I'm now developing something based on your suggestions.

analysis.insight_summary: Users find most programming tasks with [product_name] practical and easy, except working with analog multiplexers, which are considered difficult based on current examples. They want to set operational values like motor RPM counts dynamically using input switches but have trouble finding suitable samples for this scenario in available resources.
analysis.user_expectations: Users look for an intuitive method to select and assign preset values to a counter using multiple switches. They wish for simpler and more accessible logic blocks or example resources for such configurations.
